references.text: The context where Israel is called God's firstborn son, which forms the basis of the warning in verse 23
The fulfillment of the threat that all the firstborn in Egypt will die
The actual execution of judgment on Egypt's firstborn, including Pharaoh's son
Moses explains why the firstborn are to be consecrated to the Lord, referencing the judgment on Egypt's firstborn
Hosea quotes that God called his son out of Egypt, linking this to Israel as God's firstborn
God's command to Pharaoh to let the people go so they may serve Him
Pharaoh repeatedly refuses to let the people go, fulfilling the description 'you refuse to let him go'
Repeated warning about consequences if Pharaoh refuses to let the people go
Matthew applies the prophecy of God's son called out of Egypt to Jesus Christ
Theological parallel: Refusal to listen to God leads directly to a death sentence.
Contrast in God's judgment: Immediate punishment for refusal (Exodus) versus delay due to humility (1 Kings).
Direct theological connection: God's claim on the firstborn as judgment (Ex 4) and legal statute (Ex 22).
Contrast in the 'father-son' relationship: Death for refusal (Exodus) versus discipline for covenant faithfulness (2 Sam).
